in1.question: Does that match what you thought we were building?
in1.selected: Yes, that is what I pictured

n1.section: The words we will all use
n1.question: Marta is listed at Bergman as their operations lead. She has never logged in and we have not switched her access on. What is she?

n2.section: The words we will all use
n2.question: Is Customer the right word for the companies we work for?
n2.selected: Account is more natural for us

n3.section: The words we will all use
n3.question: "Assessing the car when it comes back from a rental" — what is that?

n4.section: The words we will all use
n4.question: And "check the fuel level", which happens inside that assessment — what is that?

n5.section: The words we will all use
n5.question: Does "App" work as the word for a big customer goal, or should we change it now?
n5.selected: Call it an Area of work
n5.notes: Because we see both cases where an app becomes bigger and holds many area of work inside. Not everytime a new app is the right thing. Often we have an app with 10 areas of work (modules)

n6.section: The words we will all use
n6.question: A client emails asking whether they could get a weekly summary report. What do we create in the system?

n7.section: The words we will all use
n7.question: Our Figma subscription needs renewing. What is that?

n8.section: The words we will all use
n8.question: We need the client to send us their brand logo before we can continue. What is that?

n9.section: The words we will all use
n9.question: You just spent forty minutes fixing that returns filter. What records those forty minutes?

n10.section: The words we will all use
n10.question: Which of these words feel wrong, confusing, or like they would be misread in a client meeting?
selected: Engagement
n10.notes: I dont understand what engagement would hold or track

n11.section: The words we will all use
n11.question: Is there something we do most weeks that has no word on this list?

n12.section: The words we will all use
n12.question: We dropped the idea of Phases inside sprints. A sprint now holds stories directly, with nothing in between. Right call?
n12.selected: We will miss phases — we do work in stages

ap1.question: You open the agency app at nine in the morning. What do you most want on that first screen?
selected: What I am supposed to work on today
Where each customer's sprint stands

ap2.question: A client opens the portal. What should hit them first?
selected: What we are working on right now
The status of what they asked for
ap2.notes: I believe that during a blueprint or sprint phase, it's more important for the customer to see the status of the work rather than the hours and money saved so far. These metrics become only relevant over time, once the initial project is done.

ap3.question: What are you using today for this kind of work?
selected: Glide apps we built ourselves

ap4.question: What is the single most annoying part of how we track work today?
ap4.selected: Time tracking never gets done properly
ap4.notes: It's the constantly starting and ending, and changing deadlines

ap5.question: Does the agency app need to work properly on a phone, or is it a desktop tool?
ap5.selected: Desktop mainly, phone for quick things only
ap5.notes: The main thing that has to work is tasks on the phone and adding tasks.

jr1.question: Are those five states right, or is one missing?

jr2.question: The lock rule: once we touch a ticket, the client can no longer edit or re-rank it. Fair?

jr3.question: When the last story closes, the ticket flips to ready by itself and a draft reply is written for you from the story notes. Good, or unnerving?

jr4.question: Who should write the reply the client finally reads?
jr4.notes: Aurora in the beginning, later whoever did the work.

jr5.question: Should clients be able to see which of us is working on their request?
jr5.selected: Show that it is in progress, not who

jr6.question: We dropped the 5-star priority rating and kept only the client's drag-to-rank order. Enough?

vm1.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm1.question: Where does the saved number come from?
vm1.selected: An estimate we agree with the client

vm2.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm2.question: For that number to be trustworthy, what must every step record?
selected: How long it takes and how often it happens
Who does it — a person, an automation, or an AI

vm3.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm3.question: How bold should the savings numbers be?

vm4.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm4.question: Who keeps the process map up to date?
vm4.selected: We maintain it, clients look and comment

vm5.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm5.question: When should a new version of a process be recorded?
vm5.selected: Only when someone deliberately decides to

vm6.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm6.question: Awkward one: what if a process gets worse? An automation breaks, or we get it wrong, and the latest version is slower than before.

vm7.section: The map, and the number that matters
vm7.question: When a step changes from being done by a person to being done by a machine, should the system automatically create a story for that engineering work?

tm1.question: Should one person be able to run two timers at once, on two different pieces of work?
tm1.selected: Yes, allow it — real work overlaps
tm1.notes: Especially working with AI because you can do two things at the same time

tm2.question: A timer has been running for nine hours. What should happen?
tm2.selected: Stop it automatically and flag it for review

tm3.question: Be honest: would you actually use a timer?
tm3.selected: Yes, if it is one click

tm4.question: Who should be able to fix somebody else's work log?
tm4.selected: Anyone with permission to edit work logs, with a visible trail

tm5.question: Should the system ever nag about missing time?

sw1.question: When a client logs in, should they see everything belonging to their company, or only the apps they are personally attached to?
sw1.notes: We can start with the whole company view but for bigger companies this will become a request that we can have them linked to apps.

sw2.question: Files: today, an uploaded file gets a long unguessable web link that works without logging in. Anyone holding that link can open the file. Should we require login to open client files?
sw2.selected: Keep the open links, convenience matters more

sw3.question: We stop working with a customer. What should happen to their portal access?
sw3.selected: Keep read-only access to their history

sw4.question: There is no "view as this client" button. Instead we keep one permanent fake customer, with fake people, that we can genuinely log into to see exactly what clients see. Right approach?
sw4.selected: Right — fake customer, no back door

sw5.question: Should every staff member see every customer?
sw5.selected: Mostly, but money and margins stay restricted
sw5.notes: We may want to restrict editing and add functionalities when someone is not involved in a customer.

sw6.question: If something did leak to the wrong customer, what would hurt most?
selected: What we charge, and our margins
Another customer's documents or files
Another customer's process map and how they work
Contact details of people at other companies

mn1.section: What a customer sees about money
mn1.question: Which value numbers should a client see on their home screen?
selected: Hours saved per year
Money saved per year
Number of steps we removed or automated

mn2.section: What a customer sees about money
mn2.question: Should clients see their engagement commercials — what they bought and how much of it is used up?

mn3.section: What a customer sees about money
mn3.question: Awkward one: showing "budget used" invites "why is it 80% used when I only see two things done?" Is that a conversation we want the app to start?

kn1.question: What should someone realistically be able to ask this thing?
selected: What did we agree with this client, and when
How does this process work today

kn2.question: An AI answer is confidently wrong in front of a client. What protects us?
kn2.selected: Clients can ask, but answers are clearly labelled as generated

kn3.question: Who decides the folder structure inside a customer's Drive?
kn3.selected: One standard structure for every customer, created automatically

kn4.question: Calendar: sprints and client to-dos become events in a shared kwapso calendar, staff calendars are read to show who is free, and moving an event in Google moves it in the app too. Right amount?

kn5.question: There is a document per customer that the system keeps rewriting — their current systems, open and resolved requests, what changed, how their processes work. It lives in their Drive folder. How often should it refresh?

dz1.question: Which of these feel like the right neighbours for what we are making?
selected: Stripe — dense but polished and trustworthy

dz2.question: What makes software feel heavy to you?
selected: Too many clicks to do a simple thing
Slow loading

dz3.question: How much do keyboard shortcuts matter for the agency app?

dz4.question: How much explaining should the apps do — tooltips, empty-state guidance, little help notes?
dz4.selected: Light touch — a hint only where genuinely confusing

yr1.question: What worries you most about this?
selected: Data leaking between customers
It becomes so big it is never finished

yr2.question: What would make you quietly stop using it and go back to your old way?
yr2.selected: Too many steps to log simple things
yr2.notes: if its more complicated to use then a glide app

yr3.question: Is anything missing from this document entirely?

yr4.question: Anything else you want to say before we start building?
